title: [WT-02] Daemon: worktree branch policy in complete_task, workspace in get_context
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.8 and §7.2.

Objective: make the two remaining daemon reads and checks honour the attempt's pinned workspace mode (WT-01, task-6cf120a38b344e72b7bab8b9faf806f1). A resumed session's wrapper reads the mode from get_context, and a worktree completion is checked against its own task branch.

Deliverable:
- tools/getContext.ts returns workspace: { mode, path, branch, target } from the task's open attempt. The shape is identical to WT-01's claim response. A task with no open attempt gets no field.
- tools/completeTask.ts checkBranchPolicy: when the owning attempt is workspaceMode 'worktree', currentBranch must equal moe/task/<taskId>; anything else fails with BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL naming that branch. A missing currentBranch keeps today's warning path. Shared-mode attempts keep today's consolidationBranch pattern check byte-for-byte.

NOT in scope: the claim side (WT-01); finalize_attempt (WT-03); wrappers; docs (WT-17).

Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build && npx vitest run src/tools/getContext.test.ts src/tools/completeTask.test.ts
definitionOfDone: getContext.test.ts: a task whose open attempt is worktree mode returns workspace {mode:'worktree', path, branch, target} equal to the claim's; a shared attempt returns mode 'shared'; no open attempt returns no workspace field.
completeTask.test.ts: a worktree attempt with currentBranch moe/task/<taskId> completes; any other branch is refused with BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL naming moe/task/<taskId>.
completeTask.test.ts: existing shared-mode branch-policy cases pass unchanged (no edits to their assertions).
The verification command in the description exits 0.

implementationPlan.description:
get_context: serve the open attempt's workspace (design doc docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §7.2).

This builds on WT-01 (task-6cf120a38b344e72b7bab8b9faf806f1), which must be DONE before this row is claimable. Read its landed code first: ExecutionAttempt.workspaceMode in types/schema.ts, plus the claim response's `workspace` in tools/claimNextTask.ts and the ONE pure builder that produces it. The agreed name is `attemptWorkspace(attempt, settings)`, exported from tools/claimNextTask.ts. It returns { mode, path, branch, target }, and a record with no workspaceMode reads as 'shared'. If WT-01 landed different names, use WT-01's. Never write a second copy of the rule.

getContext.ts:
- Add a top-level `workspace` key to `body`, beside currentCandidate and executionPolicy. It must be inside `body`, so the packetManifest and the packetId digest cover it.
- Its value is the claim's builder applied to currentAttempt(state, task.id) and state.project.settings. Do NOT re-derive mode, branch or target in this file.
- Error handling: read the attempt under the file's existing `decoded(...)` guard, as executionPolicyContext does. If the record cannot be read, omit the field and never throw; servedContext already reports identity-unreadable for that case.
- No task, or no open attempt (none at all, or only closed ones): no `workspace` key. Omit it, never null, following the currentCandidate precedent.
- Serve it to every role in both the default and full views: do not add it to ROLE_OMITTED. view:'status' (contextStatus) stays unchanged.

getContext.test.ts: add a new describe block. Claim through the real claim (claimNextTaskTool with statuses ['WORKING'] and workerId 'worker-1' on a WORKING task), so the assertions compare against the claim's own output:
(a) settings.worktreeMode 'on' plus consolidationBranch 'trunk'. Assert ctx.workspace toStrictEqual(claim.workspace) AND toStrictEqual({ mode: 'worktree', path: <the open attempt's stored workspace>, branch: 'moe/task/task-1', target: 'trunk' }). Also assert that path differs from projectPath. Then set the live setting to 'off' (in memory is fine) and read again: mode must still be 'worktree', because it comes from the attempt, not the setting.
(b) setting absent: ctx.workspace toStrictEqual(claim.workspace) and toStrictEqual({ mode: 'shared', path: h.state.projectPath, branch: null, target: null }).
(c) an attempt opened with openAttempt WITHOUT workspaceMode (a pre-WT-01 record) reads as mode 'shared'.
(d) no open attempt: test both a WORKING row that was never claimed and a row whose only attempt was closed (release_task or closeOpenAttempts). Assert expect(ctx).not.toHaveProperty('workspace').
Build every path with path.join or take it from the stored attempt; never hand-write a slash string. Existing tests stay unchanged.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented guarded attempt workspace inside body with WT-01 resolveAttemptWorkspace, absent without a readable open attempt. Added real-claim default/full, pinned/corrupt-live-mode, shared/legacy, closed/no-task and corrupt-attempt coverage. RED 4 expected failures (workspace absent); GREEN getContext.test.ts 55/55. Verification in HEAD Linux snapshot /tmp/wt02-gate.* with lock-matching hardlinked native dependencies and docs; only task files overlaid. Pre-existing/peer dirty paths untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
complete_task: worktree branch policy keyed on the owning attempt (design doc §2.8).

completeTask.ts checkBranchPolicy:
- Keep its call site and order: it runs before setAttemptPhase('finalizing') and updateTask, so a refusal leaves the task WORKING with no verification and the attempt 'running'.
- Pass in, or read, the task's open attempt with currentAttempt (already imported). Get its workspace from WT-01's builder (see step 1).
- When the mode is 'worktree', expected = the builder's branch (moe/task/<taskId>). This arm runs BEFORE the consolidationBranch read and its `if (!pattern) return null`: it applies whether or not consolidationBranch is set, and it never consults that pattern.
- Error handling for the worktree arm:
  - Missing, blank or non-string currentBranch: today's warning path, unchanged. Same warning text, same rate-limited #governors post (which now names the expected branch, and whose failure never blocks the completion); return { pattern: expected, matched: null, warning }.
  - Trimmed currentBranch !== expected, compared by exact case-sensitive string equality (NOT matchesBranchPattern, no prefix test): throw new MoeError(MoeErrorCode.CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, 'BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL: ...', { currentBranch, expectedPattern: expected }, 'CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION'). That is the same code, codeName and context keys as the shared refusal, so existing parsers read both.
  - The message names the reported branch, "moe/task/<taskId>" and the attempt's worktree path, and says the attempt runs in worktree mode. Do NOT reuse describeBranchPolicyFailure: its advice to peel onto moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD> is wrong in worktree mode.
  - Match: return { pattern: expected, currentBranch, matched: true }.
- Every other attempt (workspaceMode 'shared', absent on a pre-WT-01 record, any unknown value, or no attempt at all) takes today's path, with identical behavior: same pattern source, same glob matcher, same message and context.
- Update checkBranchPolicy's doc comment and the inputSchema currentBranch description to state the worktree rule.

completeTask.test.ts: add a new describe block next to 'consolidationBranch policy'. Reuse its setupMoe/writeEpic/writeTask/boot helpers and VERIFICATION, and call resetBranchPolicyGovernorRateLimit in beforeEach. Open the attempt after boot with openAttempt(state, { taskId: 'task-1', workerId: 'worker-a', runnerId: 'worker-a', workspace: path.join(testDir, '.worktrees', 'task-1'), workspaceMode: 'worktree' }). WT-01 adds workspaceMode to OpenAttemptParams; only if it did not, write that attempt JSON into .moe/attempts/ before state.load(). Cases:
1. consolidationBranch 'moe/work-*', currentBranch 'moe/task/task-1': status REVIEW; branchPolicy toEqual { pattern: 'moe/task/task-1', currentBranch: 'moe/task/task-1', matched: true }.
2. consolidationBranch 'moe/work-*', currentBranch 'moe/work-2026-07-31' (a branch the shared check accepts): refused.
   - CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION; the message contains 'BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL' and 'moe/task/task-1' and does not contain 'moe/work-<YYYY-MM-DD>'.
   - context toEqual { currentBranch: 'moe/work-2026-07-31', expectedPattern: 'moe/task/task-1' }.
   - The task is still WORKING with no verification, and the attempt phase is still 'running'.
3. No consolidationBranch, currentBranch 'main': refused, naming moe/task/task-1.
4. it.each near misses, each refused the same way: 'moe/task/task-2', 'moe/task/task-10', 'moe/task/*', 'Moe/task/task-1'.
5. No currentBranch: REVIEW, matched null, warning contains 'not enforced', and exactly one #governors post, containing 'moe/task/task-1'.
6. Two attempts under consolidationBranch 'moe/work-*' with currentBranch 'moe/task/task-1', one with workspaceMode 'shared' and one opened without workspaceMode. Both are refused with the shared context { currentBranch: 'moe/task/task-1', expectedPattern: 'moe/work-*' }.
Do not edit any existing test's body or assertions (DoD 3). Only add tests, and imports if needed.
implementationPlan.note: Added exact owning-attempt worktree branch arm before the shared consolidation check; reuses WT-01 builder, trim, warning text and global governor rate window. Shared arm remains textually intact. Dedicated helper intentionally preserves that compatibility arm (existing 300-line monolithic file now 341 lines); new helpers <=50 lines. RED 11 expected failures; GREEN completeTask.test.ts 73/73. Added trimmed match, near-miss/glob/case rejection, no-policy rejection, disk-byte no-write checks, missing/blank/non-string warnings, warning-post failure, absent/unknown/shared mode checks. Existing assertions unchanged.

comments.content:
Architect correction (plan revision 1, steps 1, 2 and 4 amended): WT-01 published its final contract in #general msg-591400ac after this plan was submitted.
- The workspace builder is `resolveAttemptWorkspace(attempt, settings)`, exported from state/validators.ts. It returns `AttemptWorkspace` (types/schema.ts), reads mode and path from the attempt, takes target from `resolveWorktreeTarget(settings)`, and never throws.
- `openAttempt` takes an optional `workspaceMode`.
- planningNotes and executionContract (reuse, approvedScope) still name `attemptWorkspace` in tools/claimNextTask.ts. That name is superseded: follow the amended step text.
- Never call `resolveWorktreeMode` in get_context or complete_task. The mode is pinned on the attempt, and that helper throws on a hand-edited setting.
- If WT-01's landed code differs from msg-591400ac, the landed code wins. Never duplicate the rule.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: get_context returns a top-level `workspace` { mode, path, branch, target }, built by the claim's own builder from the task's open attempt: equal to the claim's, with no key when there is no open attempt. complete_task's branch policy, for an open attempt whose workspaceMode is 'worktree', requires currentBranch === 'moe/task/<taskId>' whatever consolidationBranch says, and otherwise fails with BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL naming that branch; a missing currentBranch keeps today's warning path. Every other attempt, and every task without one, keeps today's consolidationBranch check unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: A worktree-mode claim followed by get_context yields workspace toStrictEqual the claim's { mode:'worktree', path:<attempt workspace>, branch:'moe/task/<id>', target }; flipping the live setting afterwards does not change the mode.
A shared claim yields { mode:'shared', path: projectPath, branch: null, target: null }; an attempt without workspaceMode reads as shared; no open attempt yields no workspace key.

A worktree attempt completes on moe/task/<id> and is refused (CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL naming moe/task/<id>, context {currentBranch, expectedPattern}) on any other branch, including a consolidationBranch match and near misses; the task stays WORKING and the attempt running.
Existing shared-mode branch-policy tests pass with no edits to their assertions.
invariants: Shared mode, meaning any attempt whose workspaceMode is not 'worktree' or a task with no attempt, behaves exactly as before (epic rail 4).
A refused completion writes nothing: the task stays WORKING, verification unset, the attempt running.
Mode, branch and target have one definition, WT-01's builder; neither tool re-derives them or reads the live worktreeMode.
get_context never throws on an unreadable attempt record; it omits workspace instead.
compatibility: BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL keeps code CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, codeName 'CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION' and context keys currentBranch/expectedPattern.
The get_context change is additive: one new top-level key, absent without an open attempt; the view:'status' payload is unchanged.
Attempt records written before WT-01 (no workspaceMode) read as shared.
approvedScope: getContext.ts: body.workspace (built with WT-01's builder over currentAttempt) inside the decoded guard.
completeTask.ts: checkBranchPolicy worktree arm, its doc comment, and the inputSchema currentBranch description.
New describe blocks in getContext.test.ts and completeTask.test.ts.
reuse: WT-01's workspace builder (agreed: attemptWorkspace in tools/claimNextTask.ts).
getContext.ts's decoded() guard, and completeTask.ts's existing missing-branch warning path and governor rate limit.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/completeTask.ts checkBranchPolicy(state, taskId, currentBranch) returns null when consolidationBranch is unset and is awaited before setAttemptPhase/updateTask.
packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts currentAttempt returns the one open (running/finalizing/reconciling) attempt, detached, or null.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Re-deriving branch and target in getContext.ts: rejected. It would create two definitions that drift, while the DoD asks for get_context to equal the claim. Use WT-01's one builder (agreed in #general msg-27e3d734: attemptWorkspace(attempt, settings), exported from tools/claimNextTask.ts).
2. Reading the live settings.worktreeMode in get_context or complete_task: rejected. §7.2 pins the mode per attempt, so a settings flip must not change an in-flight task's contract. Tests prove this by flipping the setting after the claim (get_context) and by never setting it at all (complete_task).
3. matchesBranchPattern for the task branch: rejected. The contract is exact equality, and a glob or prefix test would accept moe/task/task-10 for task-1.
4. Moving the worktree failure text into util/branchPolicy.ts: rejected to keep the task at its 4 files. The text stays inline, and the tests assert its tokens.
5. Adding workspace to view:'status': not needed; the wrapper's resume preload uses the default read.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Attempts:
- currentAttempt(state, taskId) (state/attemptStore.ts) returns the task's one open attempt (running, finalizing or reconciling) as a detached copy, or null.
- openAttempt builds the record field by field, so WT-01 must add workspaceMode to OpenAttemptParams for it to persist.
- Records load raw (loadEntities), so a pre-WT-01 record simply lacks the field.

complete_task:
- checkBranchPolicy runs before setAttemptPhase('finalizing') and updateTask, so a refusal changes nothing.
- The shared arm returns null when consolidationBranch is unset. The worktree arm must sit before that early return.

get_context:
- `body` is assembled, then packetManifest is appended, then servedContextIdentity hashes the packet. A field added inside `body` is digested; delta/receipt tests diff whole packets and are unaffected by a static field.
- The decoded(unreadable, name, fn) guard is the error-handling idiom for hand-edited attempt records.

Build and tests:
- tsconfig excludes *.test.ts from npm run build, so a test-only type error does not fail the build. Behavior assertions are the guard.
- No snapshot tests exist; the only Object.keys shape assertion (getContextDelta) is on delta responses.
- Nothing outside the daemon parses BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL or expectedPattern; it was grepped across scripts/ and the plugins.
planningNotes.risks:
WT-01 contract names:
- The builder name and module, OpenAttemptParams.workspaceMode, and whether `target` is computed live or pinned were agreed in chat while WT-01 was still being planned.
- Check WT-01's landed code before editing. If its names differ, use WT-01's and never duplicate the rule.
- If WT-01 exported no builder (inlined it in the handler), stop and comment on this task: a one-line export would edit claimNextTask.ts, which is outside this plan.

Test environment:
- vitest cannot start in the WSL shared checkout because node_modules is the Windows install. Use a Linux-node_modules snapshot that includes docs/ (otherwise the role-trim test fails on a missing docs/roles), or Windows-native npx.
- Parity-check runs on a HEAD snapshot of scripts/, so a peer's mid-edit wrapper bytes cannot fail this row.

Shared files:
- WT-01 and WT-03 are planned in parallel. WT-03 edits types/schema.ts and finalizeAttempt.ts, but neither touches this plan's 4 files.

Hand-edited attempts:
- A record whose workspaceMode is neither 'worktree' nor absent is treated as shared (today's check). That is deliberate: there is no new refusal surface for out-of-contract records.
